requirements.text: Initial project provisioning shall succeed only for a human principal admitted by the operator Access policy; a project owner who is not an operator shall receive a clear denial.
Adding one human member shall grant that verified principal the assigned project role from multiple devices after personal authentication.
Revoking one project membership shall block that principal from the project on the next protected operation across all devices.
Revocation from one project shall not remove the same principal from other projects.
Membership mutation shall preserve final-owner protection and shall not allow a principal to grant a role higher than its own.
Project and membership lookups shall preserve tenant isolation and shall not disclose project existence to unknown or non-member principals.

A teammate's first protected use shall authenticate against the coordination service, after which the service verifies existing membership; teammate authentication shall never carry provisioning authority.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 Decisions: Teammate first use, Provisioning authority

requirements.text: Onboarding guidance shall present cloud membership and Git repository access as separate prerequisites for canonical Markdown collaboration.
Local-only project creation and existing-ticket editing shall remain backward compatible when the cloud management capability is present but unused.
The effective trusted-origin set shall combine distribution-provided HTTPS service origins with operator-configured exact-HTTPS extensions; arbitrary repository-provided origins shall be denied.

Initial provisioning shall require the operator Access audience; the provisioning endpoint shall come from a trusted distribution or operator service profile, never repository data; teammate and normal operations shall use only the coordination audience.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 Decisions: Provisioning authority, Service endpoints

requirements.text: Membership, roles, and revocation shall be project-scoped; a principal's standing in one project shall not imply standing in another, and final-owner and no-self-elevation protections shall hold across mutations.
Cloud project membership and Git-host repository access shall be independent; the system shall not provision or imply Git-host permissions.
A principal who authenticates successfully through Access but is not a member of the project shall be denied on the next protected operation with non-disclosing behavior.
A lost device whose user remains a valid member shall not grant cloud access from its local session or journal; revoking the member shall block that device on the next protected operation.

A member revoked while another device still holds a valid Access session shall be blocked on that device's next protected operation via the per-operation cloud membership check; the client shall not cache or bypass the revoked membership.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 Edge: revoked with live session; AC-F7

requirements.text: One device opening multiple cloud-bound projects with different memberships shall keep independent bindings, counters, and projections with no cross-project leakage.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 Edge: multiple projects one device

requirements.text: A teammate with cloud membership but no Git repository access shall complete cloud operations while Markdown/Git collaboration is surfaced as a separately documented prerequisite.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 Edge: member without Git access; AC-F11

requirements.text: Provisioning a cloud project from one installation shall return one stable cloud project UUID; another installation or clone shall connect explicitly to that UUID without provisioning another project.

Repository configuration shall contain no cloud service origin and shall not select or redirect the privileged provisioning endpoint; the provisioning endpoint shall come only from the effective trusted service profile.
The shipped trusted service profile shall let a new clone connect to an existing cloud project without project reprovisioning or repository configuration changes.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 AC-F14; Decisions: Origin trust, Clone onboarding

requirements.text: The CONFIG_DIR connection record shall be written only after provisioning or connect and membership verification succeed; a failed readiness, provisioning, connect, or membership step shall leave connection state unchanged.

Retrying the same initial provisioning request with the same idempotency key and request content shall return the same cloud project UUID and shall not create a duplicate project; conflicting key reuse shall be rejected.

A legacy repository project.cloudSync binding shall be imported into CONFIG_DIR only through an explicit migration; migration shall not silently edit repository files and shall reject a conflicting CONFIG_DIR connection.

A teammate shall join through personal Access authentication and an explicit connect to the existing cloud project UUID without entering a shared project password or copied token; the coordination service shall verify existing project membership.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 AC-F5; Decisions: Clone onboarding, Teammate first use

requirements.text: Machine members shall have project-scoped roles while each runtime stores its own service-token credentials in an owner-only CONFIG_DIR credential file; the secret shall never enter repository configuration or the membership API.
A new or replacement installation shall connect to an existing project membership after authentication without counter, membership, or projection migration.

Device-local credentials, sessions, connection records, journals, locks, and caches shall never create a cloud project implicitly, grant a role, or define cloud project identity; connection state may select cloud operation only after cloud verification.

Disabling a cloud-bound project shall suspend coordination and retain a disabled CONFIG_DIR connection record so new ticket creation remains fail-closed; only the separately acknowledged permanent-detach procedure may resume local allocation.

The cloud project UUID, membership set, number counter, and projection namespace shall be project-scoped cloud authorities; CONFIG_DIR state may select a connection but remains non-authoritative for identity, membership, and numbering.

No cloud credential or reusable join secret shall be persisted in repository-controlled files, browser storage, logs, or project registry data; machine service-token credentials may persist only in owner-only atomic files under CONFIG_DIR/cloud-sync/credentials, and human Access tokens remain managed by cloudflared.

Machine membership shall be project-scoped while each runtime has a distinct CONFIG_DIR credential record with owner-only permissions; machine secrets shall never enter the membership API or repository-controlled state.
The same human principal using an already provisioned cloud project from two connected devices concurrently shall resolve the same cloud project UUID and membership with no session conflict.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 Edge: same user two devices

requirements.text: A CONFIG_DIR connection with an untrusted or changed service origin shall fail closed; no credential shall be sent to the untrusted origin and repository data shall not redirect provisioning.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-201 §4 Edge: untrusted or changed origin

requirements.text: When the initial provisioning response times out, retrying with the journaled idempotency key and identical request content shall return the original cloud project UUID; changed request content shall be rejected.

When a legacy repository project.cloudSync binding exists, explicit migration shall import it only if CONFIG_DIR has no connection or the same connection; a conflicting connection shall fail without modifying either source.
Readiness, provisioning, membership, CONFIG_DIR connection state, diagnostics, and disable behavior shall be exposed through one reusable management service/API with no presentation logic.

Shared services shall own readiness, provisioning, membership, CONFIG_DIR connection state, diagnostics, and disable semantics; presentation adapters shall only parse input and render output and shall contain no lifecycle business logic.

Repository-controlled files and the registry entry CONFIG_DIR/projects/{localProjectId}.toml shall contain no cloud enablement, cloud project UUID, service origin, or credential; each installation shall store its connection separately under CONFIG_DIR/projects/{localProjectId}/cloud-sync.toml.

The device-local connection record shall live at CONFIG_DIR/projects/{localProjectId}/cloud-sync.toml and contain only version, state enabled or disabled, cloudProjectId, serviceOrigin, and pollIntervalSeconds; repository files and CONFIG_DIR/projects/{localProjectId}.toml registry entries shall contain none of these cloud connection fields.

scenarios.title: Unknown and non-member principals get the same non-disclosing response
scenarios.given: A principal who is not a member of a project and a reference to an unknown project
scenarios.when: The principal queries project or membership state
scenarios.then: The same non-disclosing response is returned for unknown and non-member cases and no project existence is disclosed

scenarios.title: Local-only projects are unchanged when the cloud capability is present
scenarios.given: A project with no cloud binding while the cloud management capability is present but unused
scenarios.when: Tickets are created and edited locally
scenarios.then: Creation and editing behave identically to before the cloud management capability existed

scenarios.title: Revocation is project-scoped and protects the final owner
scenarios.given: A principal who is a member of two cloud projects and an owner of one of them
scenarios.when: The owner revokes the principal from one project, attempts to remove or demote the final owner, and attempts to grant a principal a role higher than the owner's own
scenarios.then: The revoked principal is blocked on the next protected operation in that project only and remains a member of the other project, the attempt to remove or demote the final owner is rejected, and the attempt to grant a role higher than the actor's own is rejected

scenarios.title: Provision retry and explicit connect resolve one UUID
scenarios.given: An operator-admitted human principal, a local project with no CONFIG_DIR connection, a shipped trusted service profile, and a journaled provisioning idempotency key
scenarios.when: The principal provisions the project, retries the same request after a simulated lost response, and a second installation explicitly connects using the returned cloud project UUID
scenarios.then: The retry returns the original UUID without a second cloud project, the first CONFIG_DIR connection is written only after verification, and the second installation connects to the same UUID without provisioning or changing repository files

scenarios.title: Non-operator owner cannot bootstrap provisioning
scenarios.given: A human principal who is a project owner but is not admitted by the operator Access policy
scenarios.when: The principal attempts to provision the cloud project
scenarios.then: Provisioning is denied with a clear operator-authority message and no CONFIG_DIR connection record is written

scenarios.title: Repository config cannot carry cloud state or redirect provisioning
scenarios.given: A clone whose repository configuration contains attempted cloud enablement or a service origin that differs from the trusted service profile
scenarios.when: Provisioning or connect evaluates the trusted service profile and local CONFIG_DIR state
scenarios.then: Repository cloud fields are rejected or ignored as legacy migration input, the privileged endpoint comes only from the trusted profile, and all active connection fields are written only under CONFIG_DIR

scenarios.title: Owner adds human and machine members at project scope
scenarios.given: A project owner, an enabled CONFIG_DIR connection, and a machine runtime with its own service-token pair
scenarios.when: The owner adds a human principal and the machine principal id with project roles, and the machine installs its credential pair into the runtime CONFIG_DIR credential store
scenarios.then: The human role works from any personally authenticated device, the machine role is project-scoped, the credential file is owner-only, and the secret never enters the repository or membership request

scenarios.title: Teammate explicitly connects by personal authentication
scenarios.given: A provisioned cloud project UUID and a teammate already added as a human member
scenarios.when: The teammate authenticates personally on a new installation and connects using the cloud project UUID without any shared password or copied token
scenarios.then: The coordination service verifies membership, writes the installation's CONFIG_DIR connection, and uses existing counters, memberships, and projections without provisioning or migration

scenarios.title: Device-local state never grants identity or membership
scenarios.given: A device holding a CONFIG_DIR connection, credentials, session, journal, and cache, and a teammate authenticating to the coordination service
scenarios.when: A protected project operation is attempted relying on that device-local state
scenarios.then: The local connection selects the cloud path but identity, membership, and provisioning authority are decided by the cloud per-operation check; local state never creates a project or grants a role

scenarios.title: Disable retains state and never silently resumes local numbering
scenarios.given: A cloud-bound project with an enabled CONFIG_DIR connection
scenarios.when: The owner disables the project through the management service
scenarios.then: Cloud coordination is suspended, the local connection remains present with state disabled, new ticket creation fails closed, and no local allocator is selected

scenarios.title: Legacy repository binding migrates explicitly without hidden edits
scenarios.given: A project with a legacy repository project.cloudSync binding and either no CONFIG_DIR connection, the same connection, or a conflicting connection
scenarios.when: The operator requests legacy binding migration
scenarios.then: A missing connection is imported after verification, an identical connection is a no-op, a conflict fails closed, and repository files are never edited without a separate explicit acknowledgement

scenarios.title: One reusable management contract exposes the lifecycle with no presentation logic
scenarios.given: The reusable cloud project management contract consumed by presentation adapters
scenarios.when: Readiness, provisioning, membership, CONFIG_DIR connection, diagnostics, and disable operations are invoked through the contract
scenarios.then: All lifecycle behavior is exposed through one reusable contract, and adapters only parse input and render output with no lifecycle business logic

obligations.title: Provisioning requires the operator Access audience and is denied to a project owner who is not an operator; an audience-aware credential resolver selects operator for provisioning and coordination for all other operations

The provisioning endpoint and operator audience come from a trusted service profile (distribution defaults plus operator exact-HTTPS extensions); repository data cannot select or redirect them, and the profile composes with the existing coordination-origin allowlist
Onboarding guidance documents cloud membership and Git-host repository access as separate prerequisites and names the disable and recovery procedures
Revocation takes effect on the next protected operation across all devices via the per-operation cloud membership check; it is project-scoped; the client does not cache or bypass a revoked membership

CloudProject and MembershipRecord remain cloud-authoritative; each installation keeps a non-secret CONFIG_DIR connection record with an explicit enabled or disabled state, while repository files and the project registry contain no cloud connection
Disable suspends cloud coordination, persists state disabled without deleting the CONFIG_DIR connection, and makes allocation fail closed; ordinary disable never resumes local numbering
Verification uses a local two-client integration contract plus a required manual smoke through the reusable service against the live Access-protected Worker; no browser or CLI E2E belongs to MDT-201
CONFIG_DIR connection and credential state may select a cloud path but never create a project implicitly, grant a role, or define identity; unknown and non-member lookups remain non-disclosing
Only complete absence of a CONFIG_DIR cloud connection selects local-only behavior; a disabled or invalid connection fails closed, while genuinely local-only creation and editing remain unchanged

Each machine runtime atomically stores its own Access service-token pair under CONFIG_DIR/cloud-sync/credentials with owner-only permissions; membership requests carry only the non-secret machine principal id
Human and machine principals are managed through the project-scoped members API; final-owner and no-self-elevation protections hold, and machine secrets never enter membership requests

Repository files, project registry, browser-facing DTOs, and logs contain no cloud credentials; human tokens remain with cloudflared and machine secrets persist only in owner-only atomic CONFIG_DIR credential files

A teammate explicitly connects an installation to the existing cloud project UUID using personal Access authentication; connect verifies membership, writes CONFIG_DIR state commit-last, and never provisions
Initial provisioning requires a journaled idempotency key; D1 returns the original cloud project UUID for an identical retry and rejects the same key with changed request content
Legacy repository project.cloudSync state is read only as explicit migration input; import writes CONFIG_DIR after verification, rejects conflicts, and never silently edits repository files

Tests lock CONFIG_DIR state selection, provisioning idempotency, credential-file permissions and redaction, trusted-profile origin denial, explicit connect, legacy migration conflicts, and per-operation revocation; live Access onboarding is a manual gate
One reusable CloudProjectManagementService exposes readiness, provisioning, explicit connect, membership, CONFIG_DIR state, diagnostics, disable, and migration with no presentation logic

CONFIG_DIR project connection state is written commit-last after provisioning or connect plus membership verification; absent means local-only, enabled selects cloud, disabled remains fail-closed; project cloudSync selectors are removed from normal configuration
